5. Where the full positive construction still fails to close

There is a useful norm advantage for a measured-law approach. For an  $s$ -qubit Hermitian correction  $X=2^{-s}A$ ,

 $\sum_y|\operatorname{Tr}(M_yX)|
\le\|X\|_1
\le\|A\|_{2,\tau}.
\tag{18}$ Unconditioned measurement therefore avoids an exponential support penalty.

A normalized pin has a different bound:

 $|\tau(AQ)|\le2^{s/2}\|A\|_{2,\tau}$ for  $Q=2^s|y\rangle\langle y|$ . Equation (18) cannot serve as a uniform relative likelihood estimate at rare outcomes.

A generative method could avoid relative pin estimates altogether. But I did not construct the needed globally consistent signed law with a proved  $L^1$  error and polynomial-bit prefix contractions. The native example above shows why summing absolute activities or truncating total order does not supply it.

The primary alternatives checked also require additional structure. Helmuth–Perkins–Regts’ polymer sampler assumes nonnegative weights with relative evaluation; its complex-weight counting theory does not directly sample signed activities. Midha et al.’s tensor-network construction uses quantitative strong injectivity, established for fixed-depth circuits only above a sufficiently strong noise threshold.
